text:
maria: Heads-up — p2-prod hit a string of GPU OOMs this morning that correlate with aggressive KV-cache eviction during batching spikes. nsys traces show repeated cudaMemcpy D2H/H2D (hot loop), which looks like KV pages being spilled and reloaded within the same request window.

sam: Can you paste the minimal nsys snippet or the call pattern you saw?

maria: Sure — trimmed nsys stack:
```
cudaMemcpy(dst=host_buf, src=kv_page_gpu, size=8MB)  // D2H
cudaLaunchKernel(...)  // do work
cudaMemcpy(dst=kv_page_gpu, src=host_buf, size=8MB)  // H2D
// repeat ~6-12x per token step in some traces
```
This matches the spike windows that OOM'd when concurrent batches went > 18 requests.

devon: That repeated D2H/H2D is the worst-case for latency and peak GPU memory. Two obvious levers: async spill (background, limited concurrency) and preferring to evict cold KV pages only. Do we have per-page hotness counters?

maria: We have an LRU-ish allocator for KV slots but it's coarse (per-slot, not per-page). Hotness metric is basically access count per slot in the last N tokens, but it decays slowly. When batch compaction kicks in we end up thrashing.

zach: We should also track spill backpressure in the scheduler. Right now the runtime treats spill as free; we need kv_spill_inflight limit so too many concurrent spills don't saturate PCIe. Metric suggestions: kv_spill_inflight, kv_spill_bytes/sec, kv_spill_latency.p50/p95.

sam: Agreed. Also consider a two-tier reservation: small pinned GPU-resident hot reservoir + larger soft pool that can be spilled. That way logits/activation buffers for in-flight short requests don't get evicted.

maria: Proposed short-term patch:
- add concurrency cap (default 2) for D2H/H2D spill tasks per GPU
- mark recently used KV pages as "sticky" for X ms (soft pin) to avoid immediate rehydrate
- if queue_depth > threshold, favor smaller batches / skip prefetch to reduce working set

I'll put up a PR with a config flag: runtime.kv.spill_concurrency and runtime.kv.sticky_ms.

devon: For correctness, ensure sticky is soft: when memory pressure is critical we still evict. Also precompute expected spill bytes for a batch before admitting it — admission control.

zach: We need a perf/regression test. Sam, can you add a synthetic reproducer which cycles hot/cold keys and ramps concurrency? Ideally a small harness that runs in CI perf (nsys) and fails if kv_spill_latency.p95 > X ms or OOM occurs.

sam: Yep. I'll add a harness that does 1) warm-up filling KV, 2) ramp to 24 concurrent chat requests with interleaved long contexts, 3) measure spill ops. I'll wire it into the nightly perf job.

ci-bot: perf job started: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/kv-spill/356789 (logs will attach when done)

maria: Implementation notes for the PR: keep CPU copy threads as a bounded worker pool; don't block inference scheduler threads on D2H/H2D. Use a small reservation bitmap to prevent double-evicting pages still referenced by inflight requests.

devon: Another idea: compress KV pages to reduce PCIe bytes. LZ4 for cold pages could cut spill volume by ~3x in traces we saw. Adds CPU cost but reduces transfer latency and OOM risk. Worth an experiment.

zach: Good call. Let's gate compression behind a flag runtime.kv.compress_on_spill. Start without it for stability.

sam: I'll create the perf ticket: PERF-evict-backpressure and include the nsys trace + the reproducer.

maria: Thanks — I'll open the PR today. Quick todo: add metrics + canary on one pool (canary driver) before cluster rollout. :thumbsup:

zach: :+1:
